neighbours.label: the conjunction 'but' (and 'so') joining a second instruction or consequence after a comma in advice or practical prose, as against the same sentences split into two
fire: Give the puppy small treats, not whole biscuits, but keep them for training.
Water the seedlings daily, not twice a day, but check the soil first.
Use the spare room for guests, not storage, but keep a shelf free.
You must be home by six, so plan your errands early.
Offer the children fruit, not sweets, but let them choose which.
Wear the boots around the house, not outside yet, but tie them firmly.
The lift is broken today, so take the stairs on the left.
Add the salt slowly, not all at once, but taste as you go.
quiet: Give the puppy small treats. Keep them for training.
Water the seedlings daily. Check the soil first.
Use the spare room for guests. Keep a shelf free.
You must be home by six. Plan your errands early.
Offer the children fruit. Let them choose which.
Wear the boots around the house. Tie them firmly.
The lift is broken today. Take the stairs on the left.
Add the salt slowly. Taste as you go.
